about.text: A historic water-based paint, also called casein paint, made from milk, slaked (hydrated) lime and pigment. Oil was often added to make a stronger emulsion, and recipes called for many other additives to improve durability. It was used on interiors and also on exterior surfaces.

links.name: US National Park Service, Preservation Brief 28

how.text: Curdled skim milk gives the casein; slaked lime dissolves it into a binder. Use soon after mixing.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: 1 gal of nonfat milk is left warm a few days to curdle.

steps.name: dissolve
steps.note: The curds are dissolved with 2½ oz of Type S lime in 2½ cups of water.
6 cups of whiting, plus earth pigment.
